blocks.text: Build a small client pipeline: UI layer (control, preview, status), a validator/preprocessor (type/size/dimensions + optional resize), an UploadManager (queue, progress, cancel, retry), and a thin API client for getting upload URLs. The UI is just a state machine driven by that pipeline.

Boundary checks:
- A clear state model instead of ad-hoc booleans.
- A predictable data flow (select -> validate -> preprocess -> upload -> finalize).
- Separation of concerns: UI, validation/preprocess, upload manager, API client.
- Awareness of object URL lifecycle (create + revoke).
- Main-thread safety for image work (worker/offscreen when possible).

blocks.code:
Native file input / drop enhancement
  -> attempt coordinator
  -> declared-type, size, signature-policy, and decoded-dimension validation
  -> object-URL preview + optional preprocessing
  -> upload-session client
  -> byte transfer with abort
  -> idempotent finalization
  -> durable asset callback

Attempt identity guards every asynchronous result. AbortController instances and workers live in a runtime registry, not serializable store state.

blocks.title: High-level pieces
rows: State machine
Tracks attemptId, file, previewUrl, status, progress, session, asset, error
The eight fields are the single source of truth; every visual state derives from them.
Control area
File input + optional dropzone
Handles onChange / onDrop, forwards the File object into validation, remains keyboard-accessible.
Preview area
Displays thumbnail when there is a valid previewUrl
Keeps aspect ratio, responsive layout, hides itself in idle/error states.
Status bar
Shows indeterminate or byte progress, retry, cancel, finalizing, or complete state
Progress updates should be throttled to avoid re-render storms.
Actions
Replace / Remove buttons
Replace opens picker again, Remove clears state and revokes object URL.
Validation + preprocess
Pure helpers or worker
Keep resize/compress off the main thread when possible.
Upload manager
Queue, progress, cancel, retry
Encapsulates async upload behavior and exposes lifecycle events.

blocks.title: Architecture decisions
items: Use a single, explicit status field plus progress instead of many booleans.
Isolate validation and preprocess in helpers/worker.
Keep an UploadManager with cancel/retry and progress callbacks.
Use URL.createObjectURL only after validation passes, and revoke old URLs on replace/remove.
Make size/type limits configurable via props, so the component is reusable.
Throttle progress updates to avoid re-render storms.

blocks.title: Avoid
items: Mixing file validation, preview logic, and JSX all in one huge handler.
Never revoking object URLs, causing memory leaks on long sessions.
Hiding errors behind console logs instead of user-visible messages.
Tightly coupling the component to a specific backend API (keep the upload URL step abstract).
Using only icons or color to show errors or statuses (poor accessibility).
Relying solely on click interactions and ignoring keyboard/focus flows.

steps.title: 1. Handle file selection/drop
steps.text: On input change or drop, pass the file into validation before touching state.

steps.title: 2. Validate + preprocess
steps.text: If validation passes, create a preview and optionally resize/compress (off-thread).

steps.title: 3. Upload with progress
steps.text: Request a pre-signed URL, start upload via UploadManager, and emit progress updates.

steps.title: 4. Complete or retry
steps.text: After transfer, enter finalizing. Only an authoritative UploadedAsset moves the attempt to complete and triggers onChange; a retry reuses user intent but receives fresh runtime cancellation resources.

steps.title: 5. Replace / remove
steps.text: Replace restarts the flow; remove cancels upload, revokes preview URLs, and resets state.

items.label: Core state fields
items.helperText: attemptId, file, previewUrl, status, progress, session, asset, error.

items.label: Main transitions
items.value: idle -> validating -> preprocessing -> requesting-upload -> uploading -> finalizing -> complete
items.helperText: With explicit cancelled and error recovery paths.

blocks.title: Upload pipeline ownership
blocks.text: This is not just a widget; it is a client pipeline. If you can describe UI -> preprocess -> upload manager -> finalize, you are speaking system design language.
Worked example: replacement while the first upload is finalizing
The user selects photo A, its transfer finishes, and finalization is pending when the user replaces it with photo B. A late result for A must not overwrite B or leak A’s object URL.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: A is selected
Create attempt a1, validate, and allocate one object URL.
Preview A appears in reserved geometry.
One attempt owns each local resource.
A transfer completes
Move a1 to finalizing and retain its idempotency key.
Progress becomes processing rather than falsely complete.
Transfer is not durable asset completion.
B replaces A
Abort a1, revoke A preview, create attempt b1.
Preview B appears and controls follow b1.
Current selection is identity-based.
A finalize resolves late
Ignore because a1 is obsolete; optionally issue cleanup contract.
B remains untouched.
Late callbacks cannot cross attempts.
